body:
Thanks for the catch.

One thing is that right now, the ZSH init of starship is written so that you can run `eval $(starship init zsh)` inside a clean copy of ZSH with no modules loaded (e.g. one started with `zsh -f`) and it will work.

Using `add-zsh-hook` breaks this because you then then need to `autoload` some stuff, and I'm not sure how comfortable I am `autoloading` things on behalf of the user (e.g. if we try to load a module that isn't compiled in their specific version of ZSH, the entire init becomes unusable).

I think I would prefer to use this as a springboard to create another init function (e.g. `starship init zsh --gen-zsh-prompt [path]` or something) that creates the ZSH-style prompt files. However, if we can show that the add-zsh-hook function is always autoloadable, even when e.g. ZSH was compiled with modules and the modules are now missing, then maybe we could autoload it for the user in the main init script.
